To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
modified lipid extraction methods can be developed and optimized for the recovery of microbial lipid biomarkers in deep subsurface black shale.
1) The mBD + Phosphate buffer + POPC extraction method is more reproducible and has the highest yield of lipid biomarkers compared to all other methods tested in this research.
the modified Bligh and dyes (mBD + phos + POPC) and the Folch extraction methods are the most efficient in the recovery of microbial lipids in deeply buried shale samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an efficient methodological approach to extract lipid biomarkers from deeply buried black shales, which can be used to estimate biomass and characterize the diversity of microbial community.
the development of a customized method for lipid extraction from the highly complex shale matrix.
the development and testing of a modified lipid extraction method that is suitable for the analysis of deeply buried shale samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

all the three lipid extraction methods tested are capable of extracting microbial lipids from the shale samples, but the mBD +Phos + POPC extraction method is recommended as the most reliable and reproducible for future studies.
there is no single extraction method which could consistently and reproducibly extract all lipid biomarkers from deeply buried shale samples.
there is no one extraction method that can be used to extract lipids from deeply buried shale, and the mBD + phos + POPC method is the most reproducible method tested here.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified Bligh and Dryer extraction method (mBD + phospholipase C and phosphatidylcholine) is the most effective extraction method in the recovery of lipid biomarkers from deeply buried shales.

the lipid biomarker yields in shale are highly variable across extraction treatments, and that the mBD +Phos + POPC is the best extraction treatment for the recovery of lipid biomarkers, although further methodological improvements are needed.

the mBD + POPC method has a potential for the recovery of intact phospholipids from deeply buried shales and the Folch, and the MAE methods can be used for total lipid extraction from the shale matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all lipid extraction method for deeply buried shale.
the lipid extraction methods can be customized to the specific properties of the sample, and that there are no “best” extraction methods for all samples.
the mBD + POPC treatment can be a good starting point for lipid extraction from shale samples and further method development.
